cause_quote: The dispatcher added `if (operatorScopes?.includes(ADMIN_SCOPE) && !syntheticScopes?.includes(ADMIN_SCOPE)) { syntheticScopes?.push(ADMIN_SCOPE); }`, restoring administrator authority even when a native request explicitly supplied a narrower scope array.
user_saw: An operator could explicitly narrow a native Gateway request and still have it run with administrator permissions.
summary: The fix distinguishes implicit method minimums from explicit scope ceilings and carries the effective ceiling through nested calls, agent launches, and delayed continuations.
reasoning: I checked the parent of #128548: native requests forced a synthetic client, and its constructor kept the supplied scope array, including an empty array. #128548 added the administrator grant after filtering the requested scopes, breaking that existing ceiling. The later session-scope projection and continuation changes retained or reused this behavior.
